correctness.rationale: For all integer q>=2 the vector field is C1, H is conserved and each negative regular level is a smooth cylinder with no equilibria. The coarea surface form satisfies L_X omega=-(|x|^q)omega; Stokes rules out both contractible cycles and distinct essential cycles. The Poincare multiplier is exp(-integral |x|^q dt) strictly in (0,1), and the full monodromy has the two unit multipliers of flow and first integral. Exact anisotropic scaling makes this multiplier energy-independent; Poincare-Bendixson yields convergence for every bounded forward orbit. The proof does not assert universal boundedness. The existence for q=2,3 is an explicit published theorem, with q=4..100 based on its separately credited computational corollary.

value.rationale: The original article devotes substantial analytic work to proving merely that every negative-energy level admits at least one cycle. This result settles whether there might be other cycles, proves global convergence for the entire bounded part of each leaf, and supplies an exact, parameter-invariant transverse Floquet observable, thereby upgrading an existential infinite-geometry statement to a sharp phase-portrait and stability law. This is more than restating energy homogeneity or computing a textbook coordinate substitution.
